items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: I ran into the bands of Alphonso Trent, Clyde Love, no, Clarence Love, what's this other -- Tee Holder.

ctx.x: Who else came through there? Oh. Barron Lee. It was a band out of, say, something like the Southern part of the South. I don't know exactly which state. Then there was Carmite Thompson, who was a trumpet player out of Dallas, Texas. He was a rather young man. And these bands I heard constantly, like, weekends on the domestics' nights off.

Then, we went back to Oklahoma in '29. And these same bands was coming through Oklahoma. And when I got to Oklahoma, I ran into the bands of Alphonso Trent, Clyde Love, no, Clarence Love, what's this other -- Tee Holder. And the local bands, which was two, one and two -- of course, there were others, but the number one band was Ernie Fields. And he had a trumpet player with him then -- this was like '31. And this kid was 21, and his father was a bandmaster and had a band of his own. His name was Fred Skinner. And…
